subject: FinCorp - Redwood evals setup & model recommendations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@fincorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FinCorp - Redwood evals setup & model recommendations

Hi John — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your evaluation running on Redwood: 

Recap (30-min discovery):
- Primary goal: ensure FinCorp search & summarization assistant meets accuracy and hallucination thresholds for financial guidance workflows.
- Current dataset: ~3k anonymized Q&A pairs extracted from internal KB and support logs.
- Constraints: PII-sanitized, latency target ~400ms p50 for single-turn generation, batch throughput for nightly scoring.
- Risk areas: high sensitivity to hallucination on regulatory paragraphs; need regression alerts during model swaps.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) I’ll send our eval template (CSV) and a recommended scoring rubric you can use to format a 500–1,000 row seed set. Attachment: redwood_eval_template.csv
2) We’ll run an initial A/B of three model variants on a Redwood sandbox (hosted dedicated sandbox) and share benchmark report. Recommended variants below.
3) Short follow-up call to confirm ingestion format and S3 access (if you want Redwood to pull data). I’m available Mon/Tue next week.

Model recommendations (starting point):
- "llama-2-70b-chat" (q4o) — best-quality baseline for long-context finance summaries.
- "vicuna-13b-v1" (8-bit) — lower cost, good instruction-following; useful as a cost-SLO baseline.
- "redwood/optimize-7b" (quantized) — high-throughput candidate for batch scoring and caching experiments.

Scoring/quality checks I recommend for the seed eval:
- Exact-match / token-overlap for short factual Qs (where appropriate).
- ROUGE-L and BLEU for summary similarity.
- Embedding-based semantic similarity (cosine) for paraphrase tolerance with a configurable threshold.
- Hallucination checks: entity-level F1 measured against gold spans; flag any hallucinated numeric/financial values.
- Latency and token-cost per response (p50/p95), measured under representative request sizes.

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.csv (CSV template), sample prompt set, and a link to our evals doc: https://redwood.app/docs/evals

If that plan looks good I’ll drop the CSV and a short SOW draft for procurement to review.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Scoring: for the first pass we care most about hallucination reduction and precision on entity extraction (ticker symbols, regulatory clause ids). Can you confirm the hallucination checks you mentioned are automated in your eval harness or do we need to provide labelled spans?

2) Dataset format: we'll likely export from our internal QA tool. What exact CSV columns does your template require? Any recommended size for the initial seed?

3) Hosting: prefer to run on Redwood Private (VPC) but for the initial benchmarks procurement wants to see a hosted sandbox report first. Is there any limitation on models we recommended? Also procurement will need a short SOW and your SOC 2 evidence link.

Happy to join a quick call Monday 10am PT if that works.

—John
John Lee
Director of ML Ops, FinCorp
john.lee@fincorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0133
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@fincorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCorp - Redwood evals setup & model recommendations

Thanks John — answers inline and next steps.

1) Hallucination checks: Our eval harness supports both labelled-span checks and heuristic detection. For entity-level F1 you should provide gold spans in the CSV (column name: expected_entity_spans). We also run secondary heuristics (numeric plausibility, cross-check against supplied knowledge base) which can flag likely hallucinations without spans. We’ll include both in the baseline report.

2) CSV template: attached (redwood_eval_template.csv). Required columns in the template: id, input, expected_output, expected_entity_spans, tags, metadata_json. Optional: context_text, conversation_history. Recommended initial seed: 500–1,000 rows sampled to cover high-risk regulatory intents and common support queries.

3) Hosting: For the initial benchmarks we can run on a Redwood hosted sandbox (isolated tenant) and share a model_benchmark_report.pdf. Once you’re comfortable we can replicate the same runs in your Redwood Private VPC. No hard limitations on community or open models we can evaluate — we’ll validate license compatibility and provide quantized variants for cost testing.

Scoring rubric (suggested thresholds for pass/fail on seed):
- Entity F1 >= 0.88 for regulated entities (tickers, clause ids).
- Semantic similarity (embedding cosine) >= 0.78 for summaries.
- Hallucination rate <= 2% on numeric financial facts.
- Latency p50 <= 400ms and p95 <= 1200ms for 1–2k token prompts (we’ll measure under representative CPU/GPU configs).

Procurement / SOW: attached a short SOW draft (sow_draft.pdf) and I’ve included our SOC 2 summary link in the doc. I’ll also add the HubSpot deal (DF-4821) and a link to the eval docs here: https://redwood.app/docs/evals

Next:
- I’ve attached redwood_eval_template.csv and a sample prompt set. Please populate a ~500-row seed and either upload to the S3 path in the template or give us a short-term read-only S3 credentials.
- Let’s confirm Monday 10am PT for the 30-min setup call. I’ll include Neha on that call to scope the ingestion steps.

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.csv, sow_draft.pdf

Best,
Marissa
